text:
marta: Heads-up — I sketched a Grafana panel + alert rules for cross-region ECC/Xid burst detection. Want quick sanity-check before I push to staging.

joel: Nice, thanks. Can you paste the PromQL? we should avoid noisy-card flapping.

marta: pasted a couple of queries below. idea is a per-card + per-region healthscore and a suppression layer for noisy restarts.
```promql
# ECC rate per card (5m window)
sum(rate(nvidia_ecc_corrected_total{job=\"nvidia_exporter\"}[5m])) by (card, region)
/
sum(gpu_active_cards{region}) by (region)
```

samir: i'd correlate XID spikes and driver resets too:
```promql
# XID bursts + temp
(increase(nvidia_driver_xid_errors_total[10m]) > 2) and (avg_over_time(gpu_temp_celsius[card][10m]) > 78)
```

tess: prefer a composite healthscore vs single threshold ejection. propose weights: xid=0.4, ecc=0.35, temp=0.15, soft_errors=0.1. healthscore formula (normalized 0..1).
- candidate for manual drain if score < 0.6 for > 30m
- automatic drain if score < 0.25 for 15m AND ticket created

joel: how do we avoid mass drains in a region when a noisy switch or NIC causes correlated errors?

marta: two safety guards:
1) cross-card correlation check (if > 20% cards in rack spike together, mark as network/region issue and suppress ejection).
2) staged rollout: first mark as "drain-candidate" and monitor for 6h sample before scheduled replace.

ryan: add noisy-card suppression: if restart_count(card, 30m) > 2 then suppress new severity alerts for 20m and escalate to ops channel instead of auto-drain. avoids alert storm.

samir: also suggest adding a time-decay factor so old errors weigh less. i.e. exponential decay with tau=12h in the score.

marta: agreed. also thinking of a grafana panel layout: top row = region summary + region-level SLO gap, middle = per-card sparklines (ecc/xid/temp), bottom = candidate actions table (card id, score, last_seen, action).

joel: can we include cost estimate in the annotation? if we drain/replace we lose X GPU-hours. helps prioritize for low-cost vs high-cost pools.

tess: yes — add a field: estimated_gpu_hours_lost = expected_drain_time_hours * avg_concurrency(card_pool). then multiply by $/gpu-hr. show in alert annotation.

marta: ops-bot will publish an automated note when healthscore crosses auto-drain threshold. sample message below.

ops-bot: AUTO: healthscore(gpu-34)=0.22 in us-east-1 -> scheduled drain window requested. action: create-ticket(OPS-6123), annotate-graph, suppress-new-alerts(10m).

samir: let's also tune alert threshold to avoid > 1 pager per week per region. target: P(>1 high severity alert / region / week) < 0.1. use historical test on last 90d.

marta: plan: implement queries on staging dashboard (/d/staging/gpu-health), run 7-day noise analysis, then bake-off with SREs. if results look good push to prod with canary (10% of dedicated pools).

joel: LGTM. schedule a 30m sync next Tue with ops, sres, and tess. i'll bring historical noise stats. :thumbsup:

marta: thanks — i'll add the queries to the PR and include a short runbook for manual verification + rollback steps.

ryan: small nit — add a label in prometheus metrics for hardware_rev and firmware_ver so we can correlate flaky cards by revision.

marta: will do. pushing a staging panel in ~1h, pinging this thread when done.

joel: cheers.
